content_voiceover: This is the fifth edition WHO classification of MDS, and it is heavily tested, so pay close attention. WHO splits MDS into two groups. The first group is MDS with defining genetic abnormalities. MDS with low blasts and isolated 5 q deletion requires blasts under 5 percent in the marrow and under 2 percent in blood, plus a 5 q deletion alone or with only one other abnormality other than monosomy 7 or 7 q deletion. MDS with low blasts and S F 3 B 1 mutation requires the absence of 5 q deletion, monosomy 7, or complex karyotype, with an S F 3 B 1 mutation present. MDS with biallelic T P 53 inactivation allows blasts up to 20 percent, usually shows a complex karyotype, and requires either two or more T P 53 mutations, or one mutation with evidence of T P 53 copy number loss or copy neutral loss of heterozygosity. The second group is morphologically defined MDS. Hypoplastic MDS has blasts under 5 percent marrow and under 2 percent blood. MDS with increased blasts is split into I B 1, with 5 to 9 percent marrow blasts or 2 to 4 percent blood blasts, and I B 2, with 10 to 19 percent marrow blasts, 5 to 19 percent blood blasts, or the presence of Auer rods. MDS with fibrosis spans 5 to 19 percent marrow blasts and 2 to 19 percent blood blasts. There is also a footnoted category, MDS with low blasts and ring sideroblasts, defined by wild type S F 3 B 1 with at least 15 percent ring sideroblasts.
keypoints: Two WHO groups: defining genetic abnormalities versus morphologically defined
Genetic group: MDS minus 5q, MDS S F 3 B 1, MDS biallelic T P 53
Multi hit T P 53 definition drives the biallelic T P 53 category
Morphologic group: hypoplastic, increased blasts I B 1 or I B 2, and fibrosis
Auer rods or 10 to 19 percent blasts push a case into I B 2
keypoint_voiceover: Remember the two arms of fifth edition WHO MDS. Genetically defined disease includes isolated 5 q deletion, S F 3 B 1 mutation, and biallelic T P 53 inactivation, the last one allowing blasts up to 20 percent. Morphologically defined disease includes hypoplastic MDS, increased blasts split into I B 1 and I B 2, and MDS with fibrosis. The key exam trigger is Auer rods or blasts reaching 10 to 19 percent, which automatically classifies a case as I B 2.
